sources.source_chapter_or_section: Virata Parva, SECTION VI ("Thy eternal abode is on Vindhya--that foremost of mountains. O Kali, O Kali, thou art the great Kali, ever fond of wine and meat and animal sacrifice")

verification.notes: Virata Parva SECTION VI addresses the same goddess as Kali and the great Kali in the verse that places her abode on the Vindhya.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Virata Parva, SECTION VI ("Durga, the Supreme Goddess of the Universe, born on the womb of Yasoda... the terrifier of Kansa, and the destroyer of Asuras... her who ascended the skies when dashed (by Kansa) on a stony platform, who is the sister of Vasudeva")

verification.notes: Virata Parva SECTION VI calls the goddess born of Yasoda the sister of Vasudeva, who ascended the skies when dashed by Kansa.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Virata Parva, SECTION VI ("And the king, desirous with his brothers of obtaining a sight of the Goddess, invoked her and began to praise her... Thus praised by the son of Pandu, the Goddess showed herself unto him")

verification.notes: Virata Parva SECTION VI has Yudhishthira invoke and hymn the goddess, who then shows herself to him.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Virata Parva, SECTION VI ("Durga, the Supreme Goddess of the Universe, born on the womb of Yasoda... the terrifier of Kansa, and the destroyer of Asuras... her who ascended the skies when dashed (by Kansa) on a stony platform, who is the sister of Vasudeva")

verification.notes: The goddess born of Yasoda and dashed by Kansa is hymned by Yudhishthira at Virata Parva SECTION VI.

note.en: The Mahabharata calls the Ribhus the gods of the gods: they take no oblations, feel neither joy nor misery, and do not change at the turning of a Kalpa.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, SECTION CCLIX ("And there dwell certain beings named Ribhus. They are the gods of the gods themselves. Their regions are supremely blessed, and are adored even by the deities")

verification.notes: Vana Parva SECTION CCLIX describes the Ribhus at length as beings whose regions are adored even by the deities.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, SECTION CCLIX ("O Mudgala, their supreme state is coveted even by the gods")

verification.notes: Vana Parva SECTION CCLIX is addressed to Mudgala, to whom the Ribhus and their supreme state are described.

note.en: The Santi Parva classes the gods by varna, counting the Ribhus and Maruts as the two original divisions.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Santi Parva, SECTION CCVIII ("The deities were formerly considered to be of two classes, viz., the Ribhus and the Maruts. Thus have the Viswas, the gods and the Aswins, been enumerated. Amongst them, the Adityas are Kshatriyas")

verification.notes: Santi Parva SECTION CCVIII sets the Ribhus and the Maruts as the two older classes of deities, then places the Adityas among them as Kshatriyas.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book III, Chapter I, note 20 ("The Vayu adds to the deities the Sadhyas, Viswas, Maruts, and gods sprung from Bhrigu and Angiras. The Bhagavata adds the Ribhus: and most include the two Aswins as a class")

verification.notes: Wilson's note 20 to Vishnu Purana Book III Chapter I records that the Bhagavata adds the Ribhus to the deities of this Manwantara.
